objectives.wording: Define core pharmacology terms and distinguish drug action from therapeutic application using examples.
Use a simulated case to weigh evidence, benefit, harm and patient preferences when selecting a medicine.
Distinguish generic, brand and scheduled designations and compare their implications for selection and cost.
Identify common formulations and delivery devices, demonstrate their use and compare advantages and limitations.
Compare route selection and demonstrate subcutaneous, intravenous, intramuscular, spinal, sublingual, rectal, intranasal and inhaled administration in appropriate simulation.
Trace absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion and predict how route changes exposure.
Compare receptor, enzyme, transporter and other mechanisms and relate them to dose–response patterns.
Use a computer simulation to demonstrate mechanisms and effects of representative prototype drugs.
Compare candidate combinations using kinetics, dynamics, synergy, antagonism and benefit–risk.
Adjust a simulated treatment plan for age, pregnancy, lactation or hepatic or renal impairment and explain each change.
Calculate or justify doses in simulated cases involving age, pregnancy, lactation or impaired renal or hepatic function.
Classify suspected adverse reactions in cases and assess causality using timing, alternatives and available evidence.
Explain the purpose of surveillance and complete a simulated adverse reaction report.
Identify clinically important interactions in a sample regimen and propose monitoring, separation or substitution as appropriate.
Compare agonists and antagonists by receptor selectivity, kinetics, effects, uses and adverse reactions.
Compare cholinergic and anticholinergic agents by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects, then demonstrate organophosphate poisoning management in simulation.
Use simulated emergencies to justify and demonstrate use of noradrenaline, adrenaline, dopamine, dobutamine or atropine as appropriate.
Compare major groups by kinetics, mechanism, indications and adverse effects.
Compare kinetics, actions, indications and toxicity and demonstrate representative administration techniques on a simulator.
Compare classes by kinetics, effects, uses and adverse reactions and distinguish their role in allergic rhinitis from symptomatic care for a cold.
Define pain, classify analgesics and compare non-opioids including NSAIDs by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects.
Build and justify a pharmacotherapy plan for a simulated case of gout.
Build and justify a pharmacotherapy plan for a simulated case of arthritis, including disease-modifying drugs.
Build and justify acute and preventive pharmacotherapy for a simulated case of migraine.
Compare general anaesthetics and premedications by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects.
Compare classes by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects and justify selection for representative cases.
Compare agents by kinetics, mechanism, uses and adverse reactions and develop a simulated plan for an uncontrolled seizure.
Compare kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and counsel a simulated patient on safe use.
Compare antidepressant classes by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and develop a simulated treatment plan for depression.
Compare antipsychotic classes by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and develop a simulated treatment plan for psychosis.
Compare agents by kinetics, effects, indications and adverse reactions and explain treatment goals and trade-offs in a case.
Compare drug classes by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and write a simulated prescription for a case of drug-induced parkinsonism where indicated.
Recognise methanol poisoning and outline its supervised management.
Distinguish chronic ethanol-related presentations from methanol poisoning and relate them to ethanol pharmacology.
Compare commonly misused drug classes, distinguish dependence from addiction and outline assessment and management.
Explain safeguards when prescribing medicines with dependence potential and recommend a response to a simulated concern.
Compare representative therapies by kinetics, effects, indications and adverse reactions and match them to the underlying disorder.
Compare coagulants and anticoagulants by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and build a simulated monitoring and adverse-effect response plan.
Compare fibrinolytics and antifibrinolytics by kinetics, targets, uses and adverse effects.
Compare mechanisms, kinetics, indications and adverse effects of major antiplatelet classes.
Map diuretic targets to nephron sites and compare their kinetics, effects, uses and adverse reactions with vasopressin and its analogues.
Compare targets, kinetics, indications and adverse effects across major classes.
Compare classes by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse reactions and justify choices in simulated diabetes, pregnancy and severe hypertension scenarios.
Compare drug options by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects, then build a simulated acute myocardial infarction plan.
Compare agents by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects and distinguish symptom relief from strategies that reduce long-term complications.
Compare antiarrhythmics by kinetics, actions, uses and adverse effects and justify drug choices in simulated supraventricular, ventricular, fibrillation and arrest scenarios.
Compare major agents by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects and identify medicines that can worsen lipid profiles.
Compare drug classes by kinetics, actions and harms and justify a stage-appropriate plan in simulated cases.
Compare suppressants and expectorants by actions, kinetics, uses and harms and explain selection for dry and productive cough.
Compare drug classes for ulcer and reflux disease and justify an ulcer regimen using its cause, expected benefits and adverse effects.
Compare prokinetics, emetics and antiemetics by kinetics, targets, clinical uses and adverse effects.
Compare drug actions, kinetics and harms and justify separate plans for acute and chronic diarrhoea in adult and paediatric cases.
Compare laxative classes by action, onset and harms and justify a plan for a representative case.
Distinguish disease-modifying treatment from symptom-directed therapy and compare actions, kinetics and harms.
Compare drug classes by kinetics, mechanism and adverse effects and justify individualized treatment and complication prevention in cases with and without obesity.
Compare antiresorptive and anabolic agents by kinetics, actions, uses and harms and justify treatment choices in male and female cases.
Compare thyroid hormone preparations and build a simulated replacement plan for hypothyroidism.
Compare antithyroid agents by kinetics, actions and adverse effects and build a simulated plan for hyperthyroidism.
Compare drugs that alter pituitary hormone release by target, indications, contraindications and adverse effects.
Compare corticosteroids by kinetics, actions, indications and harms and counsel a simulated patient on safe use.
Compare androgens and anabolic steroids by kinetics, actions, indications, contraindications and harms.
Compare drugs for erectile dysfunction by kinetics, actions, indications, contraindications and harms.
Compare oestrogens, progestins and their modulators by kinetics, actions, indications and harms.
Compare hormonal contraceptives and counsel on their correct use in a simulated consultation.
Compare uterotonics by kinetics, actions, indications, contraindications and adverse effects.
Compare tocolytics by kinetics, actions, indications, contraindications and adverse effects.
Match representative fertility medicines to their physiological targets and clinical roles.
Explain selective toxicity, drug exposure and resistance selection and apply the principles to a simulated case.
Use the local stewardship programme to explain empiric selection, review, narrowing and duration in a simulated case.
Compare sulfonamides, quinolones, beta-lactams, macrolides, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides and newer agents by kinetics, actions, uses and harms.
Build a simulated treatment plan for urinary tract infection using clinical and microbiological data and counsel on correct use.
Build a simulated treatment plan for a sexually transmitted infection using clinical and microbiological data and counsel on correct use.
Compare drug kinetics, actions, indications and toxicity and use current programme guidance to justify plans for representative treatment categories.
Compare drug kinetics, actions and harms and distinguish antimicrobial therapy from treatment of lepra reactions.
Compare agents for amoebiasis, visceral leishmaniasis and malaria by kinetics, targets and adverse effects.
Compare agents for filariasis by kinetics, targets and adverse effects.
Compare drug classes by kinetics, targets, spectrum and adverse effects.
Compare kinetics, targets and adverse effects and match agents to representative intestinal helminths.
Compare representative antiviral agents by kinetics, actions, indications, contraindications and adverse effects.
Compare antiretroviral drug classes by kinetics, actions, indications and adverse effects.
Compare classes by kinetics, actions, indications and toxicity and justify a simulated plan for mitigating treatment-related harms.
Compare representative agents by kinetics, immune targets, clinical uses and adverse effects.
Use simulated cases to distinguish initial assessment, supportive care and specific antidotes in common poisonings.
Outline assessment, supportive care and antivenom use in a simulated snakebite or sting.
Match representative chelators to metal exposures and justify a simulated plan including monitoring.
Classify vaccine types and explain principles of selection and safe use.
Select an agent for a representative purpose and explain limitations and precautions.
Compare medicines for acne, scabies, pediculosis and psoriasis and explain selection of sunscreen.
Compare representative glaucoma and other ocular medicines and explain how topical delivery affects exposure and use.
Compare evidence sources and demonstrate how to verify a current drug claim.
Role-play verifying and sharing drug information obtained from a representative or media source.
Critically appraise a promotional claim and interpret corresponding package information.
Develop and explain a personal drug list for a simulated condition using efficacy, safety, suitability and cost.
Write a clear, complete and rational prescription for a simulated case.
Review a sample prescription for errors and explain how to improve clarity, safety and appropriateness.
Apply relevant rules and ethical principles to controlled drugs, off-label use and prescribing for oneself or close contacts.
Use a simulated case to explain how genetic information can affect drug selection and dosing.
Use a simulated case to explain how treatment cost can affect drug selection.
Explain essential medicine selection and evaluate representative fixed-dose combinations and over-the-counter products.
Select when to measure drug concentrations, choose sampling time and calculate an adjusted dose from representative data.
Apply relevant regulatory principles to simulated discovery, approval or clinical-use cases.
Trace development and trial phases and explain the role of Good Clinical Practice and research.
Use teach-back and empathetic communication to explain correct medicine use in a simulated consultation.
Deliver a brief simulated patient or public explanation of safe medicine use, dependence and over-the-counter risks.
Identify barriers in a chronic disease scenario and demonstrate a conversation that supports adherence.
